subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the sum of the interior angles of any triangle?
questions.explain: The interior angles of any triangle always add up to 180°.

questions.q: What is the sum of the exterior angles of any convex polygon?
options: It depends on the number of sides
questions.explain: The exterior angles of any convex polygon always sum to 360°.

questions.q: Which formula gives the sum of the interior angles of a polygon with n sides?
questions.explain: A polygon splits into (n − 2) triangles, each contributing 180°.

questions.q: What is the formula for the area of a circle of radius r?
questions.explain: The area of a circle is π multiplied by the radius squared.

questions.q: What is the formula for the circumference of a circle of diameter d?
questions.explain: Circumference equals π times the diameter (equivalently 2πr).

questions.q: What is the formula for the volume of a sphere of radius r?
questions.explain: The volume of a sphere is four-thirds π times the radius cubed.

questions.q: What is the formula for the volume of a cylinder with base radius r and height h?
questions.explain: A cylinder's volume is the circular base area πr² multiplied by the height.

questions.q: How is a column vector that moves 3 right and 4 up conventionally written?
questions.explain: In a column vector the top number is the horizontal change and the bottom is the vertical change.

questions.q: What is the size of each interior angle of a regular hexagon?
questions.explain: The interior angles sum to (6 − 2) × 180° = 720°, so each is 720° ÷ 6 = 120°.

questions.q: When a straight line crosses two parallel lines, which pair of angles are equal?
questions.explain: Alternate angles between parallel lines are equal, forming a Z-shape.

questions.q: The perpendicular bisector of a line segment AB is the locus of points that are:
options: A fixed distance from A only
Equidistant from a line and a point
Twice as far from A as from B
questions.explain: Every point on the perpendicular bisector is the same distance from A as from B.

questions.q: What is the formula for the area of a trapezium with parallel sides a and b and height h?
questions.explain: The trapezium area is the average of the parallel sides multiplied by the height.

questions.q: What is the formula for the volume of a cone with base radius r and height h?
questions.explain: A cone has one-third the volume of a cylinder with the same base and height.

questions.q: What is the formula for the surface area of a sphere of radius r?
questions.explain: The curved surface area of a sphere is 4π times the radius squared.

questions.q: Two non-zero vectors are parallel if and only if one is:
options: A scalar multiple of the other
Equal in magnitude to the other
The reverse order of the other's components only
questions.explain: Parallel vectors point in the same or opposite direction, so one is k times the other.

questions.q: If vector AB = a and vector BC = b, what single vector is equal to a + b?
questions.explain: Following AB then BC by the triangle law gives the resultant AC.

questions.q: What is the size of each interior angle of a regular decagon (10 sides)?
questions.explain: The angles sum to (10 − 2) × 180° = 1440°, so each is 1440° ÷ 10 = 144°.

questions.q: A circle has radius 7 cm. Taking π ≈ 22/7, what is its area?

questions.explain: Adding vectors means adding matching components: (2 + 1, 3 + 4) = (3, 7).
